lines.english: Indeed, I've thought seriously about the question: can you guarantee my rent...?

phrases.meaning: is it that (used to introduce a yes/no question)
phrases.usageNote: Commonly used to form questions in French.

lesson-38.lessonTitle: Lesson 38: C’est de la part de qui ?

lines.french: Bonjour, j’essaie de joindre Alain Bolland. Est-il au bureau aujourd’hui ?
lines.english: Hello, I'm trying to reach Alain Bolland. Is he at the office today?

lines.french: Je ne sais pas, je vais vérifier. C’est de la part de qui ?
lines.english: I don't know, I'll check. Who is calling?

lines.french: Dites-lui que Madame Lacroix veut lui parler.
lines.english: Tell him that Madame Lacroix wants to speak to him.

lines.french: Je l’ai rencontré au Salon de l’automobile et j’ai pris sa carte de visite.
lines.english: I met him at the motor show and took his business card.

phrases.usageNote: Refers to an event where automobiles are displayed.

lines.french: J’ai appris qu’il est le nouveau directeur commercial pour l’Île de France.
lines.english: I learned that he is the new sales director for Île-de-France.

lines.french: Il m’a dit de l’appeler en début de semaine pour organiser une visite de vos locaux.
lines.english: He told me to call him at the beginning of the week to organize a visit to your premises.

phrases.literalTranslation: at the beginning of the week
phrases.meaning: at the start of the week
phrases.usageNote: Commonly used to refer to the start of a week in scheduling contexts.

lines.french: Je vous mets en attente. Ne quittez pas je vous prie.
lines.english: I'll put you on hold. Please don't hang up.

phrases.usageNote: Used in customer service contexts when a call is temporarily paused.

lines.french: Je regrette, mais son poste ne répond pas. Il doit être à l’extérieur.
lines.english: I'm sorry, but his extension is not answering. He must be out.

phrases.usageNote: Commonly used in contexts where someone is not available to take a call or respond.

lines.french: Je ne suis pas surpris parce que nous avons plein de travail en ce moment et l’agenda de Monsieur Bolland est plein.
lines.english: I'm not surprised because we have lots of work at the moment and Mr. Bolland's schedule is full.

lines.french: Voulez-vous laisser un message ?
lines.english: Would you like to leave a message?

phrases.usageNote: Common phrase used when asking someone to leave a message.

lines.french: Pouvez-vous lui demander de me recontacter plus tard dans la journée ?
lines.english: Can you ask him to contact me again later today?

phrases.meaning: to ask him to contact me again
phrases.usageNote: Common construction for requesting someone to get back in touch.

lines.french: Entendu. Il a vos coordonnées, je présume ?
lines.english: Understood. He has your contact details, I presume?

phrases.usageNote: Common phrase referring to someone's contact information.

lines.french: Normalement oui, mais je vais vous donner un numéro où il peut me trouver à tout moment.
lines.english: Normally yes, but I'll give you a number where he can reach me at any time.

phrases.usageNote: Common expression used to indicate availability or readiness.

lines.french: C’est le 07 28 91 12. Attendez, excusez-moi, c’est le 02 à la fin.
lines.english: It's 07 28 91 12. Wait, excuse me, it's 02 at the end.

lines.french: Si je ne réponds pas c’est parce que je suis en réunion.
lines.english: If I don't answer, it's because I'm in a meeting.

phrases.usageNote: Common phrase used to indicate being occupied in a formal gathering.

lines.french: J’ai compris. Je lui laisse votre message. Au revoir et merci de votre appel.
lines.english: I understand. I'll leave him your message. Goodbye and thank you for your call.

phrases.usageNote: Standard farewell expression in French.

lines.french: Un grand merci pour votre coopération.
lines.english: Many thanks for your cooperation.

phrases.usageNote: Commonly used to express appreciation in both formal and informal contexts.

lines.french: La France possède une longue tradition cinématographique, et le "septième art" est bien vivant aujourd’hui.
lines.english: France has a long cinematic tradition, and the "seventh art" is very much alive today.

phrases.usageNote: Commonly used to refer to cinema as an art form.

lines.french: Malgré toutes les plateformes de diffusion et tous les autres supports disponibles,
lines.english: Despite all the streaming platforms and all the other available media,

phrases.usageNote: Refers to various media platforms for content distribution.
Refers to various forms of media aside from streaming platforms.

lines.french: beaucoup de gens vont deux ou trois fois par semaine au cinéma.
lines.english: many people go to the movies two or three times a week.

lines.french: Et les metteurs en scène et comédiens français sont très appréciés par le public.
lines.english: And French directors and actors are greatly appreciated by the public.

phrases.usageNote: Common phrase indicating popularity or favor among audiences.

lines.french: Le choix de films est énorme - comédies, aventures, policiers, dessins animés, et cætera.
lines.english: The choice of films is enormous - comedies, adventures, crime films, cartoons, and so on.

phrases.usageNote: Used to indicate additional items in a list.

lines.french: Naturellement, il y a aussi beaucoup de films étrangers dans les "salles obscures",
lines.english: Naturally, there are also many foreign films in the movie theaters,

phrases.usageNote: A common term for cinemas in French.

lines.french: qu’on peut voir en version originale ou en version française (c’est-à-dire doublés).
lines.english: which one can see in the original version or in French version, that is, dubbed.

phrases.meaning: the original language version of a film
phrases.usageNote: Often used to refer to films shown in their original language with subtitles.

phrases.meaning: the version of a film dubbed in French
phrases.usageNote: Refers to films that have been translated and dubbed into French.

lines.french: Deux rendez-vous annuels sont indispensables pour les cinéphiles :
lines.english: Two annual events are essential for film lovers:

phrases.usageNote: Commonly used to refer to recurring events or meetings.

lines.french: le festival de Cannes avec sa Palme d’Or, et la soirée des Césars ;
lines.english: the Cannes festival with its Palme d'Or, and the César awards ceremony;

phrases.usageNote: Commonly used to refer to the annual film awards in France.

lines.french: ces prix récompensent le meilleur du cinéma de l’année, notamment le meilleur film et le meilleur scénario.
lines.english: these prizes reward the best of the year's cinema, especially best film and best screenplay.

phrases.usageNote: Used to refer to top achievements in film.
Commonly used in award contexts.
Used in film awards to denote top writing.

lines.french: La semaine dernière, des millions d’amateurs en ont suivi la cérémonie de clôture.
lines.english: Last week, millions of fans followed its closing ceremony.

phrases.usageNote: Refers to the concluding event of a festival or competition.

lines.french: Ils ont vu la maîtresse et le maître de cérémonie présenter les prix aux gagnants.
lines.english: They saw the mistress and master of ceremonies present the prizes to the winners.

phrases.usageNote: Commonly used in formal events and ceremonies.

lines.french: Et maintenant, le moment que nous attendons tous : le César du meilleur metteur en scène.
lines.english: And now, the moment we are all waiting for: the César for best director.

phrases.usageNote: Commonly used to refer to a significant or awaited moment.
Refers to the César award for the best in a specific category.

lines.french: Cette année il est attribué à... Michel Bonnaud pour "Commencez sans moi".
lines.english: This year it is awarded to... Michel Bonnaud for "Start Without Me."

phrases.usageNote: Used to indicate the recipient of an award.

lines.french: Essayant de rester décontracté, le gagnant répond :
lines.english: Trying to stay relaxed, the winner replies:

phrases.usageNote: Common expression used to describe maintaining a calm demeanor.

lines.french: Merci, je n’ai jamais reçu un prix de la mise en scène.
lines.english: Thank you, I have never received an award for directing.

lines.french: Mais je suis étonné car je n’ai pas tourné un seul film depuis vingt ans.
lines.english: But I am surprised because I haven't made a single film in twenty years.

lines.french: C’est justement pour ça que le jury vous donne cette récompense, mon cher Michel !
lines.english: That is precisely why the jury is giving you this award, my dear Michel!

phrases.usageNote: Commonly used to indicate a reason or justification.

lines.french: Tu veux venir avec moi au ciné ce soir ? Il y a plein de nouveautés à voir cette semaine.
lines.english: Do you want to come to the movies with me tonight? There are lots of new releases to see this week.

phrases.usageNote: Common way to invite someone to join.
Informal term for cinema.

lines.french: Où est-ce que j’ai mis le guide des spectacles ? Je l’ai perdu ? Non, le voici.
lines.english: Where did I put the entertainment guide? Did I lose it? No, here it is.

phrases.usageNote: Common phrase to ask for location.
Refers to a publication listing shows.

lines.french: Regarde : "L’Etranger du nord", c’est le dernier film avec l’acteur russe que tu aimes bien.
lines.english: Look: "The Stranger from the North" is the latest film with the Russian actor you like.

phrases.usageNote: Common way to refer to an actor's nationality.

lines.french: Bof, j’ai vu la bande-annonce. Je déteste les films d’action et, en réalité, je n’aime pas trop cet acteur.
lines.english: Meh, I saw the trailer. I hate action films and, actually, I don't like that actor very much.

phrases.usageNote: Used to clarify or emphasize a point.

lines.french: Fais un effort ! Bois ton café et aide-moi à choisir quelque chose.
lines.english: Make an effort! Drink your coffee and help me choose something.

phrases.usageNote: Common phrase used to request assistance in making a choice.

lines.french: Je l’ai bu. En fait, j’en ai déjà pris trois ce matin. As-tu une autre proposition de film ?
lines.english: I drank it. In fact, I've already had three this morning. Do you have another film suggestion?

phrases.usageNote: Common way to ask for alternatives.

lines.english: "The Old Port." The action takes place in the south of France. I've heard good reviews.

phrases.usageNote: Used to describe the setting of an event or action.

lines.french: Ah non, il est nul ce film ! Autre chose ?
lines.english: Oh no, that film is awful! Something else?

lines.french: Une comédie musicale ? Non, ce n’est pas vraiment ton truc.
lines.english: A musical? No, that's not really your thing.

lines.french: Si, si. J’en ai vu une - "Entre l’est et l’ouest" -, et elle m’a plu.
lines.english: Yes, yes. I saw one - "Between East and West" - and I liked it.

phrases.literalTranslation: Between the east and the west
phrases.meaning: A title of a musical or play
phrases.usageNote: Used to refer to a specific work in conversation.

lines.french: À quelle heure sont les séances au multiplexe du centre commercial ?
lines.english: What time are the showings at the shopping center multiplex?

phrases.usageNote: Commonly used to ask for the time of an event.

lines.french: Dans quelle salle passe le film ? Il y en a une douzaine.
lines.english: Which theater is the film playing in? There are about a dozen.

phrases.usageNote: Used to inquire about the location of a film screening.

lines.french: Il faut d’abord faire la queue ici pour avoir le tarif étudiant.
lines.english: First you have to line up here to get the student rate.

phrases.usageNote: Common expression used to indicate waiting in line.

lines.french: Comment, tu n’as pas pris les billets à la billetterie en ligne ?
lines.english: What, you didn't get the tickets at the online box office?

phrases.usageNote: Common phrase used to refer to purchasing tickets.

lines.french: Non, je suis bête. Je n’y ai pas pensé.
lines.english: No, I'm silly. I didn't think of it.

lines.french: J’ai horreur d’attendre. Allons prendre un verre quelque part.
lines.english: I hate waiting. Let's go have a drink somewhere.

phrases.usageNote: Common expression for going out for drinks.

lines.french: Allô, bonjour. Je suis bien au restaurant "La Fleur d’Argent" ?
lines.english: Hello, good day. Am I speaking to the restaurant "La Fleur d'Argent"?

phrases.usageNote: Common phrase used to refer to being at a restaurant.

lines.french: Oui monsieur. Vous y êtes.
lines.english: Yes sir. You are.

phrases.usageNote: Common phrase used to confirm someone's presence or location.

lines.french: J’essaie de vous joindre depuis deux jours. Ça sonne toujours occupé.
lines.english: I've been trying to reach you for two days. It's always busy.

lines.french: J’en suis conscient. Mais depuis que nous sommes dans le guide touristique,
lines.english: I am aware of that. But since we are in the tourist guide,

phrases.usageNote: Common phrase referring to being included in a travel guide.

lines.french: le téléphone n’arrête pas de sonner et nous sommes complets presque tous les soirs.
lines.english: the phone does not stop ringing and we are full almost every evening.

lines.french: Vous pouvez toujours essayer de réserver avec l’application MaTable.fr. C’est plus sûr.
lines.english: You can always try to book with the MaTable.fr app. It's safer.

phrases.usageNote: Commonly used when discussing making reservations.

lines.french: Oui, je connais cette appli, mais je préfère avoir une voix humaine au bout du fil.
lines.english: Yes, I know that app, but I prefer to have a human voice on the other end of the line.

phrases.literalTranslation: at the end of the line
phrases.usageNote: Used to refer to a person on the other end of a phone call.

lines.french: Comme vous voulez. Combien êtes-vous et à quelle heure souhaitez-vous dîner ?
lines.english: As you wish. How many are you and what time would you like to dine?

phrases.meaning: How many people are in your party?
phrases.usageNote: Commonly used in restaurant or reservation contexts.

lines.french: Vers vingt heures trente, pour quatre couverts. À la terrasse si possible.
lines.english: Around eight-thirty, for four place settings. On the terrace if possible.

phrases.meaning: Referring to seating outside on the terrace
phrases.usageNote: Commonly used in restaurant contexts.

lines.french: Huit heures et demie, dites-vous ? Oui, il me reste une petite table pour quatre.
lines.english: Eight-thirty, you say? Yes, I have one small table for four left.

phrases.usageNote: Commonly used in contexts of availability.

lines.french: Mais à l’intérieur, car toutes les tables dehors sont prises. Cela vous convient-il ?
lines.english: But inside, because all the tables outside are taken. Does that suit you?

phrases.meaning: A polite way to ask if something is acceptable
phrases.usageNote: Used in formal contexts to check for agreement.

lines.french: Si vous n’avez rien d’autre.
lines.english: If you don't have anything else.

lines.french: Alors je note. C’est à quel nom ?
lines.english: Then I'll write it down. Under what name?

phrases.usageNote: Used to inquire about the name under which something is registered.

lines.french: Ferré, comme le chanteur. Mais rassurez-vous : je ne chanterai pas.
lines.english: Ferré, like the singer. But don't worry: I won't sing.

lines.french: Très drôle... J’ai besoin d’un numéro de portable
lines.english: Very funny... I need a mobile number

lines.french: ainsi que les détails de votre carte bancaire, pour éviter une annulation de dernière minute.
lines.english: as well as your bank card details, to avoid a last-minute cancellation.

phrases.term: pour éviter une annulation de dernière minute
phrases.literalTranslation: to avoid a cancellation of last minute
phrases.usageNote: Used when discussing the need to prevent last-minute changes or cancellations.

lines.french: Vous voulez aussi mon chéquier, ou mes empreintes digitales peut-être ?
lines.english: Do you also want my checkbook, or my fingerprints perhaps?

phrases.usageNote: Commonly used in financial contexts.

phrases.meaning: the unique patterns of ridges on a person's fingers
phrases.usageNote: Often used in legal or security contexts.

lines.french: C’est bien ça. Vous pouvez me les envoyer par texto.

phrases.usageNote: Used to confirm understanding or agreement.

lines.english: Did you empty the wastepaper basket this morning?

phrases.usageNote: Used in formal or written French.

lines.english: Yes. Why? Have you lost something?

lines.english: I can't find my checkbook, but perhaps I forgot it at home this morning.

phrases.usageNote: Commonly used to express doubt or possibility.

lines.french: Je suis sûr que je l’ai vu quelque part. Sur votre bureau, peut-être ?
lines.english: I'm sure I saw it somewhere. On your desk, perhaps?

phrases.usageNote: Used to express confidence in a statement.

lines.french: Non, j’ai regardé mais il n’y est pas. Mais où est-ce que je l’ai mis ?
lines.english: No, I looked but it's not there. But where did I put it?

lines.english: Wait, I'm silly! I left it at reception earlier.

phrases.usageNote: Refers to the reception area in a building.

lines.french: Heureusement que vous l’avez trouvé !
lines.english: Good thing you found it!

lines.french: J’ai oublié de vous dire que Cécile Durieux, la comédienne, a appelé tout à l’heure.
lines.english: I forgot to tell you that Cécile Durieux, the actress, called earlier.

phrases.usageNote: Common phrase used when informing someone about something.

lines.english: She says she has been trying to reach you for a few days.

lines.english: Since last Tuesday, precisely. She left several messages.

lines.english: Can you call her back? Her number is 07 70 80 90.

phrases.usageNote: Common phrase used when asking someone to return a call.

lines.english: He went to high school in Nice and then went up to Paris to study at university.

lines.french: Il est entré à la faculté de droit, où il est devenu un fan de sports d’équipe.
lines.english: He entered law school, where he became a fan of team sports.

phrases.usageNote: Common phrase used to refer to attending law school.

lines.french: Un soir, il est allé voir un match international féminin entre les Pays-Bas et l’Allemagne.
lines.english: One evening, he went to see an international women's match between the Netherlands and Germany.

phrases.usageNote: Common phrase used to refer to women's sports events.

lines.french: Le jeu lui a vraiment plu et il a pris la décision de travailler comme entraîneur dans ce sport en Europe."
lines.english: He really liked the game and decided to work as a coach in this sport in Europe."

phrases.meaning: to work in the role of
phrases.usageNote: Commonly used to describe job roles or professions.

lines.french: Est-ce qu’il est rentré en Espagne ?
lines.english: Did he go back to Spain?

phrases.usageNote: Common question structure in French.

lines.french: Non, il est retourné à la fac pour étudier la gestion sportive. L’article continue :

phrases.usageNote: Informal way to refer to university education.

lines.english: before being appointed official coach of the Bordeaux women's team.

phrases.literalTranslation: to the position of official coach
phrases.meaning: to the role of head coach

lines.french: Dans ce cas, la billetterie est là-bas, vers les consignes et les Objets trouvés.
lines.english: In that case, the ticket office is over there, near the lockers and lost property.

phrases.usageNote: Common term used to refer to the place where tickets are sold.
Common term used to refer to a place where lost items are kept.

lines.french: Vous voyez les deux files d’attente devant les guichets ?
lines.english: Do you see the two lines in front of the ticket windows?

lines.french: Prenez celle de gauche : elle avance plus vite que l’autre... enfin, moins lentement.
lines.english: Take the one on the left: it moves faster than the other... well, less slowly.

phrases.usageNote: Used to refer to a specific item among options.

lines.french: C’est bon, Jules, j’ai les billets. Je vais les composter.
lines.english: It's good, Jules, I have the tickets. I'm going to validate them.

phrases.usageNote: Refers to travel tickets.

lines.french: Fais attention à ne pas les mettre dans le mauvais sens dans la machine !
lines.english: Be careful not to put them in the machine the wrong way!

lines.french: C’est énervant ! On affiche partout "Le compostage est obligatoire",
lines.english: It's irritating! Everywhere there are signs saying "Validation is mandatory,"

phrases.usageNote: Common phrase indicating a requirement.

lines.french: mais toutes les machines sont hors service et je n’ai pas pu valider les billets.
lines.english: but all the machines are out of order and I couldn't validate the tickets.

phrases.usageNote: Common expression used for machines that are not functioning.

lines.french: À ce moment-là, il faut le signaler au contrôleur à bord du train.
lines.english: In that case, you have to tell the conductor on board the train.

phrases.usageNote: Common phrase used to refer to being inside a train.

lines.french: Veux-tu de l’aide pour porter ton sac ? Il a l’air très lourd.
lines.english: Do you want help carrying your bag? It looks very heavy.

phrases.usageNote: Common phrase used when offering assistance.
Common verb construction indicating purpose.

lines.french: Non merci, il est grand mais en réalité il est assez léger.
lines.english: No thank you, it's big but actually quite light.

lines.french: Attends une minute, je regarde le tableau d’affichage des trains de grandes lignes :
lines.english: Wait a minute, I'm looking at the departures board for mainline trains:

lines.french: "Circulation perturbée : Nancy : Train en panne ; Colmar : Retard ; Mulhouse : Annulé".
lines.english: "Traffic disrupted: Nancy: train broken down; Colmar: delayed; Mulhouse: canceled."

phrases.usageNote: Used to indicate that traffic conditions are affected, often due to accidents or delays.
Commonly used to report a train that is not operational due to mechanical issues.

lines.french: Il n’y a même pas de trains omnibus ! C’est toujours la même chose et j’en ai marre !
lines.english: There aren't even any local trains! It's always the same thing and I'm fed up!

phrases.usageNote: Common expression used to emphasize the absence of something.
Common expression used to express frustration or annoyance.

lines.french: À chaque fois il y a des soucis avec ces lignes, vrai ou faux ?
lines.english: Every time there are problems with these lines, true or false?

lines.french: Je suis d’accord, mais il vaut mieux prendre notre mal en patience.
lines.english: I agree, but we'd better be patient.

lines.french: Il n’en est pas question. Je vais plutôt prendre le car !
lines.english: No way. I'm going to take the coach instead!

lesson-45.lessonTitle: Lesson 45: Il n’y a pas de métiers inutiles

lines.french: On m’a invitée aujourd’hui pour vous parler des réseaux sociaux professionnels.
lines.english: I was invited today to talk to you about professional social networks.

phrases.usageNote: Commonly used to refer to platforms like LinkedIn.

lines.french: Bien entendu, le monde du travail a changé considérablement depuis vingt ans.
lines.english: Of course, the world of work has changed considerably over the last twenty years.

phrases.usageNote: Refers to the professional environment or job market.

lines.french: Mon père, que j’admire, a travaillé toute sa vie dans la même usine,
lines.english: My father, whom I admire, worked his whole life in the same factory,

lines.french: alors que mon frère, qui a vingt-cinq ans, a déjà changé plusieurs fois d’entreprise.
lines.english: whereas my brother, who is twenty-five, has already changed companies several times.

phrases.usageNote: Used to indicate frequency of an action.

lines.french: De nos jours, on peut devenir avocat, ingénieur, journaliste, comptable ou programmeur,
lines.english: Nowadays, one can become a lawyer, engineer, journalist, accountant, or programmer,

phrases.usageNote: Commonly used to refer to the present time.

lines.french: mais aussi boucher, coiffeur, cuisinier ou plombier : il n’y a pas de métiers inutiles.
lines.english: but also a butcher, hairdresser, cook, or plumber: there are no useless jobs.

phrases.term: il n’y a pas de métiers inutiles
phrases.lemma: il n’y a pas de métiers inutiles
phrases.literalTranslation: there is not of jobs useless
phrases.usageNote: A phrase used to emphasize the value of all professions.

lines.french: Je veux vous parler de ce que je sais faire, plutôt que de ce que je voudrais faire.
lines.english: I want to talk to you about what I know how to do, rather than what I would like to do.

phrases.literalTranslation: this that I know how to do
phrases.meaning: what I know how to do
phrases.usageNote: Used to refer to one's skills or abilities.

phrases.literalTranslation: this that I would like to do
phrases.meaning: what I would like to do
phrases.usageNote: Used to express desires or aspirations.

lines.french: Je suis conceptrice multimédia et consultante,
lines.english: I am a multimedia designer and consultant,

phrases.usageNote: Common way to introduce one's profession.

lines.french: un métier qui demande une excellente formation, et pas mal de connaissances techniques.
lines.english: a job that requires excellent training and quite a lot of technical knowledge.

lines.french: Ce qui est difficile est qu’on est toujours en train de voyager : en avion, en train, parfois en bateau ;
lines.english: What is difficult is that one is always traveling: by plane, by train, sometimes by boat;

phrases.usageNote: Common way to indicate mode of travel.
Common way to indicate mode of travel.
Common way to indicate mode of travel.

lines.french: on n’arrête pas de bouger ! Nous ne pouvons pas prendre de congés,
lines.english: we never stop moving! We cannot take time off,

phrases.usageNote: Common expression for taking a break from work.

lines.french: et nous ne passons jamais assez de temps dans les villes que nous visitons, ce qui est dommage.
lines.english: and we never spend enough time in the cities we visit, which is a shame.

phrases.usageNote: Common expression indicating sufficient duration.

lines.french: Mais, bon, c’est comme ça. Et les choses changent tellement vite !
lines.english: But, well, that's how it is. And things change so quickly!

phrases.usageNote: Used to express acceptance of a situation.

lines.french: Que faites-vous maintenant, madame ? Toujours le même métier ?
lines.english: What are you doing now, madam? Still the same job?

phrases.usageNote: Common way to ask someone about their current activity.
Used to refer to one's job or profession.

lines.french: Non, je suis entre deux emplois. Ce qui veut dire que je suis au chômage.
lines.english: No, I am between jobs. Which means that I am unemployed.

phrases.usageNote: Common expression to indicate a temporary employment gap.
Used to describe someone who is not currently employed.

lesson-46.lessonTitle: Lesson 46: Depuis, je n’ai aucune nouvelle

lines.french: J’ai perdu mon mari, monsieur l’agent. Il a disparu.
lines.english: I've lost my husband, officer. He has disappeared.

lines.french: Quand l’avez-vous vu pour la dernière fois ?
lines.english: When did you see him for the last time?

phrases.usageNote: Commonly used to inquire about the most recent occurrence of an event.

lines.french: Hier matin. Nous sommes partis ensemble pour faire les courses.
lines.english: Yesterday morning. We left together to do the shopping.

phrases.usageNote: A common expression used to refer to grocery shopping.

lines.french: Moi, je suis allée à l’hypermarché près du Boulevard périphérique et lui est allé à la boulangerie.
lines.english: I went to the hypermarket near the ring road and he went to the bakery.

phrases.usageNote: Used to indicate proximity to a specific location.

lines.french: Et depuis, je n’ai aucune nouvelle, même pas un petit coup de téléphone.
lines.english: And since then, I haven't heard anything, not even a quick phone call.

lines.french: Pouvez-vous décrire votre époux, s’il vous plaît ?
lines.english: Can you describe your husband, please?

phrases.usageNote: Common polite phrase used when making a request.

lines.french: Il a une quarantaine d’années, mince et assez grand ; environ un mètre quatre-vingt-cinq.
lines.english: He is about forty, thin and quite tall; about one meter eighty-five.

lines.french: Un visage carré avec des cheveux bruns, longs et raides, et des lunettes noires.
lines.english: A square face with long, straight brown hair and black glasses.

phrases.usageNote: Common way to describe hair color.

lines.french: Comment est-il habillé ? En costume ? En jean ?
lines.english: How is he dressed? In a suit? In jeans?

phrases.usageNote: Commonly used to describe formal clothing.
Used to describe casual clothing.

lines.french: Il porte un pantalon gris et une chemise à manches courtes, une écharpe et une veste en cuir marron.
lines.english: He is wearing gray trousers and a short-sleeved shirt, a scarf, and a brown leather jacket.

phrases.usageNote: Commonly used to describe shirt types.

phrases.meaning: Referring to the material and color of the jacket
phrases.usageNote: Used to describe clothing material and color.

lines.french: Oh, et des chaussures noires et des chaussettes assorties.
lines.english: Oh, and black shoes and matching socks.

phrases.meaning: Referring to a type of footwear
phrases.usageNote: Commonly used to describe shoes.

phrases.meaning: Referring to a type of clothing accessory
phrases.usageNote: Commonly used to describe socks that match.

lines.french: Voilà une description vraiment détaillée, meilleure qu’une photographie !
lines.english: That's a really detailed description, better than a photograph!

phrases.usageNote: Used to emphasize the quality of description.

lines.french: Je peux faire mieux : j’ai un petit film sur mon téléphone. Vous voulez le voir ?
lines.english: I can do better: I have a short video on my phone. Do you want to see it?

phrases.usageNote: Common expression used to indicate an improvement in performance or quality.

lines.french: Non, ce n’est pas la peine. Vous le décrivez très bien. Mieux que moi !
lines.english: No, that's not necessary. You describe him very well. Better than me!

phrases.usageNote: Common phrase used to express approval or satisfaction.

lines.french: J’ai l’habitude de le perdre : il déteste faire du shopping et il disparaît une fois sur deux.
lines.english: I'm used to losing him: he hates shopping and disappears every other time.

phrases.usageNote: Common phrase used to indicate a regular behavior or routine.
Common expression used to refer to the activity of shopping.

lines.french: Aucun souci : nous allons faire de notre mieux pour le retrouver.
lines.english: No problem: we will do our best to find him.

phrases.usageNote: Common phrase used to express commitment to doing one's best in a situation.

lines.french: J’ai un service à te demander : peux-tu nous aider à déménager samedi et dimanche prochains ?
lines.english: I have a favor to ask you: can you help us move next Saturday and Sunday?

phrases.meaning: a favor to request from you
phrases.usageNote: Commonly used when asking someone for help or a favor.

lines.french: Je vais aussi demander à Stéphane et à Olivier : plus on est nombreux, plus on s’amuse.
lines.english: I'm also going to ask Stéphane and Olivier: the more people there are, the more fun it is.

phrases.usageNote: Used to express that having more people is beneficial or enjoyable.

lines.french: Tu vas leur demander de travailler un samedi ? Bonne chance ! Ce sont de gros paresseux.
lines.english: You're going to ask them to work on a Saturday? Good luck! They are big lazybones.

phrases.usageNote: Commonly used when asking someone to perform a task or job.

lines.french: Tu pourrais éventuellement parler à Didier, mon beau-frère : il a une entreprise de déménagement.
lines.english: You could possibly talk to Didier, my brother-in-law: he has a moving company.

phrases.meaning: to have a conversation with Didier
phrases.usageNote: Used when suggesting someone to communicate with another person.

lines.french: Est-ce que tu peux lui parler, toi ? Je ne le connais pas. Tu penses qu’il peut le faire gratuitement ?
lines.english: Can you talk to him? I don't know him. Do you think he can do it for free?

phrases.meaning: Is it that (used to form a yes/no question)
phrases.usageNote: Commonly used to introduce yes/no questions in French.

lines.french: J’en doute, car ses affaires vont mal, mais je peux toujours essayer. Je te tiens au courant.
lines.english: I doubt it, because his business is doing badly, but I can always try. I'll keep you posted.

phrases.usageNote: Used to indicate keeping someone informed or updated.

lines.french: Mon beau-frère est d’accord pour t’aider. Je lui ai dit que tu es un de mes meilleurs amis.
lines.english: My brother-in-law agrees to help you. I told him that you are one of my best friends.

phrases.usageNote: Used to express consent or agreement to do something.

lines.french: En plus, il est aimable : il te facture seulement la location du camion et une demi-journée de travail.
lines.english: Besides, he is kind: he is only charging you for the truck rental and half a day's work.

phrases.usageNote: Used to introduce an additional point or fact.
Commonly used to refer to a work period of half a day.

lines.french: En gros, cela te fait quelques centaines d’euros, au lieu de mille ou plus, son tarif normal.
lines.english: Basically, that comes to a few hundred euros, instead of a thousand or more, his normal rate.

lines.french: Il est très bien, ce Didier ! C’est très gentil de sa part. Tu peux le remercier ?
lines.english: This Didier is great! That's very kind of him. Can you thank him?

phrases.meaning: on his part; as a gesture from him
phrases.usageNote: Used to express appreciation for someone's kindness or gesture.

lines.french: Tu peux lui dire toi-même : il arrive dans une heure et demie avec un collègue. On va les attendre.
lines.english: You can tell him yourself: he'll arrive in an hour and a half with a colleague. We'll wait for them.

lines.french: Maintenant, au boulot. Tout ce qui est gros et lourd va dans le camion de Didier :
lines.english: Now, to work. Everything big and heavy goes in Didier's truck:

phrases.meaning: to work; a common expression to indicate starting work
phrases.usageNote: Often used to signal the beginning of a task or work session.

lines.french: le canapé, les fauteuils, les lits, les armoires, la machine à laver, le lave-vaisselle et la cuisinière.
lines.english: the sofa, the armchairs, the beds, the wardrobes, the washing machine, the dishwasher, and the stove.

lines.french: Le reste - la vaisselle, les tableaux, la télé, le linge, les rideaux,
lines.english: The rest - the dishes, the paintings, the TV, the linens, the curtains,

lines.french: les cartons dans l’escalier et les piles de bouquins contre le mur -
lines.english: the boxes in the stairwell and the piles of books against the wall -

lines.french: on le prend avec nous dans la camionnette. Je vais la chercher tout de suite.
lines.english: we'll take it with us in the van. I'll go get it right away.

phrases.usageNote: Common expression used to indicate inclusion in a group.
Common phrase used to indicate promptness.

lines.french: Bon courage à tout le monde : on a une longue journée devant nous.
lines.english: Good luck everyone: we have a long day ahead of us.

phrases.meaning: A phrase used to wish someone good luck or encouragement.
phrases.usageNote: Commonly used in various contexts to motivate or support someone.

lines.french: Plus vite on finit, plus vite on peut se coucher.
lines.english: The faster we finish, the sooner we can go to bed.

phrases.meaning: An expression indicating that the quicker a task is completed, the sooner one can move on to the next activity.
phrases.usageNote: Used to emphasize efficiency and speed in completing tasks.

phrases.term: plus vite on peut se coucher
phrases.lemma: plus vite on peut se coucher
phrases.literalTranslation: the sooner we can go to bed
phrases.meaning: An expression indicating that completing a task quickly allows for rest or leisure sooner.
phrases.usageNote: Often used in contexts where fatigue is a concern after a long day of work.

lesson-48.lessonTitle: Lesson 48: Ça ne me dit rien

lines.french: Comme il fait chaud aujourd’hui, nous allons pique-niquer dans la forêt de Fontainebleau.
lines.english: Since it's hot today, we are going to picnic in the Fontainebleau forest.

lines.french: Honnêtement, un pique-nique ne me dit rien. C’est tellement inconfortable.
lines.english: Honestly, a picnic doesn't appeal to me. It's so uncomfortable.

phrases.usageNote: Used to express lack of interest or desire for something.

lines.french: On est mal assis par terre et on mange mal : les chips, les salades de riz dégoûtantes,
lines.english: You sit badly on the ground and eat badly: chips, disgusting rice salads,

phrases.usageNote: Describes an uncomfortable seating position.

lines.french: des sandwichs de poulet sans goût, les bananes trop mûres - et des fourmis et des guêpes partout.
lines.english: tasteless chicken sandwiches, overripe bananas - and ants and wasps everywhere.

phrases.usageNote: Describes food that lacks flavor.

lines.french: Et puis on a du mal à manger proprement, avec les assiettes en papier, les gobelets en carton,
lines.english: And then it's hard to eat neatly, with paper plates, cardboard cups,

phrases.meaning: to eat in a tidy manner
phrases.usageNote: Common expression used to describe eating without mess.

lines.french: les fourchettes en plastique et les couteaux qui ne coupent rien.
lines.english: plastic forks and knives that don't cut anything.

phrases.meaning: knives that are ineffective or dull
phrases.usageNote: Used to describe poor quality utensils.

lines.french: Bref, je ne supporte pas les pique-niques.
lines.english: In short, I can't stand picnics.

lines.french: Mais ce n’est pas vraiment une mauvaise idée, tu sais. Au contraire.
lines.english: But it's not really a bad idea, you know. On the contrary.

phrases.usageNote: Used to downplay a statement.

lines.french: D’abord, c’est nous qui allons préparer la nourriture, avec de bons produits sains.
lines.english: First, we are the ones who will prepare the food, with good healthy products.

lines.french: Ensuite, pas de problème de confort. Regarde ceci : c’est notre nouveau panier à pique-nique.
lines.english: Next, no comfort problem. Look at this: it's our new picnic basket.

phrases.usageNote: A common expression used to indicate that something is not a concern.

lines.french: Mais ce n’est pas un panier, c’est un sac à dos !
lines.english: But that's not a basket, it's a backpack!

lines.french: Oui, mais c’est un sac à dos de luxe ! Il y a tout ce qu’il faut pour faire de vrais repas.
lines.english: Yes, but it's a luxury backpack! It has everything needed to make real meals.

phrases.usageNote: Used to describe a backpack that is stylish or expensive.

lines.french: Des couverts en métal, des assiettes en porcelaine, et des verres à vin et à eau.
lines.english: Metal cutlery, porcelain plates, and wine and water glasses.

lines.french: Et regarde cela. Qu’est-ce que tu en penses ?
lines.english: And look at that. What do you think of it?

lines.french: Qu’est-ce que c’est ?
lines.english: What is it?

lines.french: C’est un sac spécifique pour les bouteilles de vin blanc. Sophistiqué, non ?
lines.english: It's a special bag for bottles of white wine. Sophisticated, isn't it?

phrases.term: sac spécifique pour les bouteilles de vin blanc
phrases.lemma: sac spécifique pour les bouteilles de vin blanc
phrases.literalTranslation: special bag for bottles of white wine
phrases.meaning: A specific type of bag designed for carrying white wine bottles
phrases.usageNote: Useful in contexts related to wine or packaging.

lines.french: On a aussi quatre chaises pliantes, une table basse et une vraie couverture.
lines.english: We also have four folding chairs, a low table, and a real blanket.

lines.french: Mais attends, qu’est ce qui se passe ? La pluie commence à tomber.
lines.english: But wait, what's happening? The rain is starting to fall.

phrases.usageNote: Commonly used to inquire about a situation or event.

lines.french: Oh, il pleut. Quel dommage ! Pas de pique-nique aujourd’hui...
lines.english: Oh, it's raining. What a shame! No picnic today...

phrases.usageNote: Used to express regret about a situation.

lines.french: Quel est le monument le plus visité de France ?
lines.english: What is the most visited monument in France?

lines.french: Nous avons cherché sur Internet, mais il y a pas mal de réponses différentes,
lines.english: We searched on the Internet, but there are quite a few different answers,

lines.french: ce qui nous fait penser que notre question est mal posée.
lines.english: which makes us think that our question is badly worded.

lines.french: En effet, ce n’est pas la bonne question. Vous n’avez pas assez réfléchi.
lines.english: Indeed, that's not the right question. You haven't thought enough.

phrases.usageNote: Used to confirm or emphasize a statement.

lines.french: Ce qu’il faut chercher est "quel est le monument le plus visité cette année ?".
lines.english: What you need to search for is "what is the most visited monument this year?"

lines.french: Regardez l’écran : "Le Louvre reçoit plus de visiteurs que la Tour Eiffel"
lines.english: Look at the screen: "The Louvre receives more visitors than the Eiffel Tower"

phrases.meaning: an instruction to direct attention to the screen
phrases.usageNote: Commonly used in classroom or presentation settings.

lines.french: Et juste en-dessous "Le monument préféré des Français est le Château de Fontainebleau".
lines.english: And just below, "The French people's favorite monument is the Château de Fontainebleau."

lines.french: Je suis aussi surprise que vous par Fontainebleau. À mon avis, c’est certainement le Louvre.
lines.english: I am as surprised as you by Fontainebleau. In my opinion, it's certainly the Louvre.

phrases.meaning: expresses a shared feeling of surprise
phrases.usageNote: Used to indicate empathy or shared emotions in conversation.
Commonly used to express one's viewpoint.

lines.french: Moi, le musée que j’aime le plus est Orsay. Il a la meilleure collection de tableaux impressionnistes du monde.
lines.english: For me, the museum I like most is Orsay. It has the best collection of Impressionist paintings in the world.

lines.french: Peut-être, mais le Louvre est plus grand et plus intéressant. Plus je le visite, plus je le trouve superbe.
lines.english: Perhaps, but the Louvre is bigger and more interesting. The more I visit it, the more superb I find it.

lines.french: Et la Tour Eiffel ? À mon avis, c’est elle qui reçoit le plus grand nombre de visiteurs. Même moi, j’y suis allé !
lines.english: And the Eiffel Tower? In my opinion, it is the one that receives the greatest number of visitors. Even I went there!

phrases.usageNote: Used to specify or emphasize a particular subject.

lines.french: Eh non, désolée. J’ai trouvé les dernières informations qui circulent. Le gagnant est... Le Louvre !
lines.english: Well no, sorry. I found the latest information going around. The winner is... the Louvre!

phrases.usageNote: Refers to the most recent updates or news.
Used to describe information that is being shared or spread.

lines.french: Bien sûr. Nous, les Français, nous apprécions les artistes plutôt que les ingénieurs.
lines.english: Of course. We French appreciate artists rather than engineers.

phrases.usageNote: Used to refer to the citizens of France as a collective group.
Used to express preference between two options.
